The fixed 0441 entry is Gambling Cage Workers / O*NET43-3041.00, handling patron cash and chips and tickets and credit, check cashing, and bookkeeping at the cage in approved gambling jurisdictions; the jurisdiction and position authority are verified against the actual rules. In mainland China, Article 303 of the Criminal Law separately provides for criminal liability for assembling people for gambling for profit or taking gambling as an occupation, operating a casino, and organizing Chinese citizens to participate in gambling outside the country's borders reaching the statutory circumstances; Article 82 of the current Law on Public Security Administration Punishments covers providing gambling conditions for profit or participating in gambling with relatively large stakes (effective 2026-01-01). Article 3 of the Lottery Administration Regulations provides that welfare and sports lotteries are issued under franchise and that selling foreign lottery tickets within the country is prohibited; a U.S. occupation code does not confer a Chinese operating permit.

Paper exercise｜The entry module gives a complete C/V2 synthesized cage packet: versions, dual cash and chip accounts, pending credit verification status, and handover. Complete the four deliverables independently in 90 minutes and check them against the reference and the three counterexamples; do not touch real customers, accounts, venues, funds, or terminals.

Fit signals｜O*NET focus points: continuous contact with others (96% continuous contact), working with a work group or team extremely important (60%), daily face-to-face discussions (54% every day), daily decisions affecting others and organizational resources (71% every day), must be very precise or highly accurate “extremely important” (97%), continuous or almost continuous use of hands to operate and control and sense objects and tools and controls (69%), continuous or almost continuous repetitive motions (46%), daily time pressure from strict deadlines (50% every day), respondents choosing a regular schedule (91%). If you can handle cash and chip and ticket transactions quickly and accurately during peak hours, verify amounts and vouchers transaction by transaction, and adhere to recordkeeping and reporting requirements, this occupation's daily demands are closer to your working style.

Caution signals｜O*NET also shows: consequences of error “extremely serious” (50%) and “very serious” (23%) and “fairly serious” (13%), physical proximity “moderately close (within arm's reach)” (72%) and “very close” (17%), need to deal with unpleasant or angry or impolite people every day (41%), competition level “extremely competitive” (18%) and “highly competitive” (13%) and “moderately competitive” (31%), continuous or almost continuous standing (36%) or more than half the time (44%), decision freedom “some” (35%) and “limited” (20%) with another 20% very limited, and few positions use email daily (52% never). This occupation centers on cash and chips and tickets and credit and bookkeeping and compliance responsibility: one missing identity or credit or document verification, one large or unusual transaction not identified and reported, one face-value or amount or exchange error, one case of cash and chips and tickets not matching the books or being privately balanced, or one missing transaction or record can cause financial loss and compliance penalties and license risk; moreover, gambling is strictly restricted by law in mainland China, and before getting involved the law and authorization of the location must be verified. If you find it hard to stay transaction-accurate over the long term and to keep reporting in a highly regulated cash environment, these should be treated as real costs requiring careful weighing.

Assumption of judgment｜First use C/V2 to verify versions, amounts collected and paid, and dual-account differences, and to explain unapproved credit and duplicate records; the deliverables only observe how you read the rules, recalculate, and leave a trace. Real cage tasks, fund authority, background registration, and position training are verified separately, and being correct on paper does not constitute competence, health tolerance, or proof of hiring.

Direct answer｜The work of gambling cage workers can be broadly divided into three categories. First, cash and chip and ticket receipt and payment and exchange: handle receipt and payment and exchange of cash and chips and tickets for patrons, convert gambling chips and tokens and tickets to currency upon patron request, supply currency and coins and chips to other departments as needed, complete cash and coin and chip inventory recalls and rotations as needed, and complete payouts and referrals according to procedures. Second, credit and check cashing and bookkeeping settlement: accept patrons' credit applications and verify credit references to decide whether to provide check-cashing authorization or establish house credit accounts, verify the accuracy of authorization slips and transaction summaries and exchange summaries and similar reports, count funds and reconcile the daily transaction summary with the books, prepare and make bank deposits and balance allocated funds when necessary, use a cash register to record casino exchange transactions, and establish new computer accounts. Third, supply and records and collaboration: determine each window's cash needs and order the required currency and coins and chips, compile reports including company fund allocation or departmental revenue records, provide patrons with casino operating information, assist in training and onboarding new cashiers, and maintain transaction and identity and bookkeeping records and handle and report anomalies according to jurisdictional and employer procedures. The three categories of work link in cycles: determine cash needs and supply — handle receipt and payment and exchange — verify credit and check cashing — count and reconcile and deposit — record and report anomalies.

O*NET occupational profile highlights｜The official scope of O*NET-SOC 43-3041.00 “Gambling Cage Workers” is: In a gambling establishment, conduct financial transactions for patrons. Accept patron's credit application and verify credit references to provide check-cashing authorization or to establish house credit accounts. May reconcile daily summaries of transactions to balance books. May sell gambling chips, tokens, or tickets to patrons, or to other workers for resale to patrons. May convert gambling chips, tokens, or tickets to currency upon patron's request. May use a cash register or computer to record transaction. Of the 17 tasks given in the occupational profile, 12 are core tasks: keep patron transactions confidential; comply with all gambling rules; maintain cage security; cash checks for patrons and handle credit card cash advances; supply currency and coins and chips or gambling checks to other departments as needed; convert gambling checks and coupons and tokens and coins to currency upon patron request; count funds and reconcile the daily transaction summary to balance the books; verify the accuracy of authorization slips and transaction reconciliation or exchange summary reports; determine each window's cash needs and order the required currency and coins and chips; complete cash and coin and chip inventory recalls and rotations as needed; assist in training and onboarding new cashiers; provide patrons with casino operating information. There are another 5 supplemental tasks: prepare and make bank deposits and balance allocated funds when necessary; compile reports including company fund allocation or departmental revenue records; use a cash register to record casino exchange transactions; establish new computer accounts; sell gambling chips and tokens and tickets to patrons or to other workers for resale to patrons.

Credit and check cashing｜Application and verification｜Accept patrons' credit applications and verify credit references, decide whether to provide check-cashing authorization or establish house credit accounts, and verify authorization slips and related reports.

Bookkeeping and reconciliation｜Counting and balancing｜Count funds and reconcile the daily transaction summary to balance the books, prepare and make bank deposits, and compile fund allocation and departmental revenue reports.

Supply and inventory｜Ordering and rotation｜Determine each window's cash needs and order currency and coins and chips, supply other departments as needed, and complete cash and coin and chip inventory recalls and rotations.

Systems and records｜Entry and accounts｜Use a cash register to record exchange transactions, establish new computer accounts, and keep transaction and identity and bookkeeping records accurate and traceable.

Security and compliance｜Confidentiality and reporting｜Keep patron transactions confidential and maintain cage security, comply with gambling rules and anti-money laundering and customer identification requirements, and identify and report anomalies and suspicious activity according to procedures.

Boundary conclusion｜The core difference between this occupation and adjacent positions lies in “object and output”: this occupation takes cage cash and chips and tickets and credit and bookkeeping as its object and completes receipt and payment and exchange and check cashing and counting and reconciliation, with the output being verified and recorded cage funds and bookkeeping and compliance records; gambling change persons and booth cashiers produce currency and chip and ticket exchange and cashiering at the exchange window; gambling dealers produce table game operation and chip receipt and payment; gambling and sports book writers and runners produce wager acceptance and odds verification and payout records; first-line supervisors of gambling services workers produce shift scheduling and on-site supervision and performance and compliance enforcement; gambling managers produce venue operations and pricing and personnel and compliance management results; gambling surveillance officers and gambling investigators produce surveillance and investigation and compliance evidence. Core concept of adjacent positions｜Most positions in the same group and adjacent positions aim to “accurately complete funds and transactions within a highly regulated venue and maintain compliance and security,” and the difference lies in the transaction object and output: some take cage cash and chips and tickets and bookkeeping as their object, some take the exchange window and cashiering, some take games and chips, some take wager tickets and payout, some take shifts and on-site supervision, some take venue operations and compliance, and some take surveillance and investigation.

Core purpose of this occupation｜Taking cage cash and chips and tickets and credit and bookkeeping as the object, and within the scope of jurisdictional and employer permits and procedures, turn patron financial transactions into accurate receipt and payment and exchange and check cashing and counting and reconciliation and verifiable records: verify identity and credit, handle receipt and payment and exchange, verify vouchers and amounts, count and balance and deposit, report anomalies, so that funds and books are traceable and meet compliance requirements.

Main objects and basis of adjacent positions｜Gambling change persons and booth cashiers follow exchange and cashiering processes and limits; gambling dealers follow game rules and chips and table limits; gambling and sports book writers and runners follow wager tickets and odds and payout rules; first-line supervisors of gambling services workers follow scheduling and on-site supervision and compliance procedures; gambling managers follow venue operations and licensing and compliance and budgets; gambling surveillance officers and gambling investigators follow surveillance and investigation and evidence procedures.

Main object and basis of this occupation｜The objects are patron identity and age and eligibility, credit applications and credit references, cash and chips and tickets and gambling checks, the reserve and inventory and accounts, and the daily transaction summary and bank deposits and books, based on jurisdictional gambling rules and licensed venue requirements, anti-money laundering and customer identification and cash transaction reporting requirements, and employer cash and voucher and bookkeeping and security procedures.

Occupational profile｜This occupation conducts financial transactions for patrons inside the cage of a licensed gambling establishment: receive and pay cash and chips and tickets and exchange them for currency upon patron request, supply currency and coins and chips to other departments as needed and complete inventory recalls and rotations, accept patrons' credit applications and verify credit references to provide check-cashing authorization or establish house credit accounts, cash checks and handle credit card cash advances, verify the accuracy of authorization slips and transaction reconciliation or exchange summary reports, count funds and reconcile the daily transaction summary with the books, prepare and make bank deposits and compile fund allocation and departmental revenue reports, use a cash register to record exchange transactions and establish computer accounts, provide patrons with casino operating information and assist in training new cashiers, and keep patron transactions confidential and maintain cage security. Common employers include licensed casinos and gambling service operators and the cage operations departments of some horse racing and sports betting channels; the work is characterized by high-frequency cash and chip and ticket transactions during peak hours and per-transaction high precision and customer communication and a high degree of compliance, requires prolonged standing and repetitive operations, and the consequences of error can be extremely serious; the authority and qualifications involving licensing and compliance and anti-money laundering and customer identification and check cashing and credit are determined by the jurisdictional regulator and the licensed employer. Official definition text: In a gambling establishment, conduct financial transactions for patrons. Accept patron's credit application and verify credit references to provide check-cashing authorization or to establish house credit accounts. May reconcile daily summaries of transactions to balance books. May sell gambling chips, tokens, or tickets to patrons, or to other workers for resale to patrons. May convert gambling chips, tokens, or tickets to currency upon patron's request. May use a cash register or computer to record transaction.

Responsible parties for adjacent positions｜Responsibility for positions in the same group and adjacent positions is usually defined by the affiliated licensed institution and jurisdictional regulatory rules and compliance systems, and the objects of responsibility are mostly the institution and customers and funds and the regulator.

The definition of this occupation includes accepting credit applications and verifying credit references to provide check-cashing authorization or establish house accounts, so specific positions may have judgment authority; anomalies and overreach are escalated through institutional pathways, and it is not the case that all individual decisions are excluded or that every transaction requires regulatory confirmation.

values: C/V2 complete synthesized input

C/V2 anonymized paper packet, with cash in abstract units and chips in pieces, each piece with a face value of 10 as a problem setting only, with no real operations. V2 replaces V1: R1 actually collected 200 and issued 20 pieces, V1 mistakenly wrote 220 collected. Opening cash 1000 / chips 100, closing actual count cash 640 / chips 83. R2 recalled 15 pieces and actually paid 150; D1 actually allocated cash 100 and 10 chips to a department; B1 actually deposited 300; A1 credit application 70 lacking approval, no payment made and no chips issued; R2 repeat scan, the original transaction is complete and no further receipt or payment is made.

Draft X used V1 and recorded 220 collected, counted the pending approval of 70 for A1 as actually paid, repeated R2 and paid 150 again and collected 15 pieces again, and wrote closing cash 500 and chips 100, covering the difference with another window's money; these are not the correct results. Pen and paper, a calculator, and a spreadsheet with 90 minutes are enough; no real terminal is needed.
90-minute dual accounts and reference

90 minutes: 15 verify version, 25 dual accounts, 20 status, 15 handover, 15 counterexample; deliver the four items — version input / dual-account formulas / transaction status / handover — keeping X's original and the reasons for change. Correct cash: actually collected 200, actually paid 150+100+300=550, should be 1000+200-550=650, actual 640 minus book 650 = -10; net outflow 350 = 1000-650 = 550-200. Chips: 100-20+15-10=85 pieces, actual 83 minus book 85 = -2 pieces; the problem-setting face value difference of -20 abstract cash units is only a chip valuation and cannot be used to offset the cash difference of -10.

X's five errors: V1, treating pending approval as paid, repeating R2, the cash figure 500 being inconsistent with the erroneous formula 1000+220-150-100-300-70-150=450, and privately covering the difference. The chips figure of 100 is merely the erroneous value after counting the 15 collected twice; unknowns are not filled in.
Three status counterexamples

Counterexample 1: A1 approved but unpaid is still 650/85; a synthesized new version actually paying 70 gives cash 580 / chips 85, and if the actual count is still 640/83 the cash is +60 and chips -2. Counterexample 2: R2 repeated is not counted and is still 650/85; if the erroneous 150 is paid again and 15 are collected, the book becomes 500/100, which is only an erroneous scenario and not an operating plan.

Counterexample 3: a new version in which D1 actually returns cash 100 and 10 pieces should be 750/95; if the actual count is still 640/83 the differences are -110/-12. Cash and chips are accounted separately, and chip valuation is not used to offset cash; keep the new version conditions and do not treat the counterexamples as the original problem.
Paper task boundaries

Everything is anonymized and synthesized, with no real customer ticket or account or venue transactions; the credit lacking approval is a problem-setting pending-verification status, and the deliverables only write a handover to the synthesized supervisor role and do not actually file anything. The deliverables observe the approach and do not confer qualifications or receipt and payment authority.

entries.answer: According to O*NET-SOC 43-3041.00, this occupation conducts financial transactions for patrons inside a gambling establishment: accept patrons' credit applications and verify credit references to provide check-cashing authorization or establish house credit accounts, may reconcile daily summaries of transactions to balance the books, may sell gambling chips and tokens and tickets to patrons or to other workers, may convert chips and tokens and tickets to currency upon patron request, and may use a cash register or computer to record transactions. The work includes cashing checks for patrons and handling credit card cash advances, supplying currency and coins and chips to other departments as needed, counting funds and reconciling the daily summary, verifying authorization slips and transaction reconciliation and exchange summary reports, determining window cash needs and ordering currency and coins and chips, completing cash and coin and chip inventory recalls and rotations, preparing and making bank deposits and compiling fund allocation and departmental revenue reports, using a cash register to record exchange transactions and establishing computer accounts, providing patrons with casino operating information, assisting in training new cashiers, and keeping patron transactions confidential and maintaining cage security. What this page describes is a legal position in jurisdictions such as the United States that allow licensed gambling; in mainland China, apart from the state-approved lotteries issued in accordance with the law, gambling and operating casinos are strictly prohibited by the Criminal Law and other laws.

entries.answer: The core difference lies in object and output: this occupation takes cage cash and chips and tickets and credit and bookkeeping as its object and completes receipt and payment and exchange and check cashing and counting and reconciliation, with the output being verified and recorded cage funds and bookkeeping and compliance records; gambling change persons and booth cashiers produce window exchange and cashiering and counts; gambling dealers produce table game operation and chip receipt and payment; gambling and sports book writers and runners produce wager acceptance and odds verification and payout records; first-line supervisors of gambling services workers produce shifts and on-site supervision and performance and compliance enforcement; gambling managers produce venue operations and licensing and compliance management; gambling surveillance officers and gambling investigators produce surveillance and investigation and evidence. The objects and outputs differ, and the authority for release and credit and fund handling cannot be carried over across positions.

subject.summary: Gambling Cage Workers (O*NET-SOC 43-3041.00, Gambling Cage Workers) conduct financial transactions for patrons inside the cage of a gambling establishment: accept patrons' credit applications and verify credit references to provide check-cashing authorization or to establish house credit accounts; may reconcile daily summaries of transactions to balance the books; may sell gambling chips and tokens and tickets to patrons or to other workers for resale to patrons; may convert chips and tokens and tickets to currency upon patron request; and may use a cash register or computer to record transactions. The work includes cashing checks for patrons and handling credit card cash advances, supplying currency and coins and chips to other departments as needed, counting funds and reconciling the daily summary, verifying authorization slips and transaction reconciliations and exchange summary reports, determining window cash needs and ordering currency and coins and chips, completing cash and coin and chip inventory recalls and rotations, preparing and making bank deposits and compiling fund allocation and departmental revenue reports, using a cash register to record exchange transactions and establishing computer accounts, providing patrons with casino operating information, assisting in training new cashiers, keeping patron transactions confidential, and maintaining cage security. Official definition text: In a gambling establishment, conduct financial transactions for patrons. Accept patron's credit application and verify credit references to provide check-cashing authorization or to establish house credit accounts. May reconcile daily summaries of transactions to balance books. May sell gambling chips, tokens, or tickets to patrons, or to other workers for resale to patrons. May convert gambling chips, tokens, or tickets to currency upon patron's request. May use a cash register or computer to record transaction.
